claims.text: Replacing X with Si in CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of a dual-layer oxide scale.
The proposed dual-layer scale consists of an inner Cr-rich oxide and an outer Si-enriched glassy layer.
The dual-layer structure minimizes lattice and thermal-expansion mismatch at the metal/oxide interface.
The Si-induced scale grows slowly and remains coherent above 900 °C.
The Si-induced scale resists cracking and spallation above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Mn or Al do not form an equally effective protective bilayer.
The proposed behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
The relevant intervention is substitution of X by Si, with X = Mn and X = Al alloys used as comparisons.
The intended domain includes oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C under isothermal and thermal-cycling conditions.
A continuous, compositionally graded Cr-rich/Si-rich oxide promotes chemical inertness and mechanical integrity at the interface.
Silicon produces a self-healing dual-layer oxide structure.
The inner Cr-rich oxide bonds strongly to the metallic substrate.
The outer Si-rich glassy layer limits oxygen diffusion.
Limiting oxygen diffusion and reducing thermal-expansion mismatch suppresses stress buildup, cracking, and spallation.
Si-containing alloys will show slower scale thickening, less cracking and spallation, and greater mechanical robustness than corresponding Mn- or Al-containing alloys.
Previous reports found unstable, cracking, and spalling oxides in CrFeCoNi alloys without Si or with Mn or Al additions.
Failure of the Si alloy to show a significantly more coherent, slower-growing, and mechanically robust scale than the Mn and Al controls would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that silicon enhances oxidation kinetics, while the hypothesis and predicted outcome assert slow scale growth and oxygen-diffusion limitation. This may be reconcilable if 'enhances' refers only to rapid establishment of the protective bilayer, but that distinction is not stated.
